sentence: A Vernier caliper with 20 VSD equal to 19 MSD (1 MSD = 1 mm) has a least count of _______.
explanation:
LC = 1/n × MSD = 1/20 × 1 mm = **0.05 mm** ✓

Verification: 1 VSD = 19/20 mm = 0.95 mm → LC = 1 − 0.95 = 0.05 mm

instruction: Match each instrument to its typical least count:
explanation:
Metre scale: least count = smallest graduation = 1 mm.
Vernier (10): LC = 1/10 mm = 0.1 mm.
Vernier (20): LC = 1/20 mm = 0.05 mm.
Screw gauge: LC = 1/100 mm = 0.01 mm (10× finer than Vernier).

title: Absolute Error & True Value

sections.heading: What is the True Value?
sections.body:
We can never know the exact true value.

Instead, we take the **arithmetic mean** of n repeated measurements as our best estimate:

**ā = (a₁ + a₂ + ... + aₙ) / n**

sections.heading: Absolute Error
sections.body:
For each measurement aᵢ:

**Δaᵢ = |aᵢ − ā|**

Always take the **absolute value** — errors are never negative.

sections.heading: Mean Absolute Error
sections.body:
Average all individual absolute errors:

**Δā = (Δa₁ + Δa₂ + ... + Δaₙ) / n**

Final result reported as: **(ā ± Δā)**

This means the true value likely lies between ā − Δā and ā + Δā.

highlight: Mean absolute error = our uncertainty. The true value is within ā ± Δā with high confidence.

title: Absolute → Relative → Percentage Error

parts.meaning: Mean absolute error (same units as quantity)
Mean (best estimate) of the measured quantity

note: Relative error has no units. It tells you what fraction of the value is uncertain.
derived_from: Relative error = |uncertainty|/|value|. Multiply by 100 to express as percentage.

question: Five measurements of a length are: 2.62, 2.63, 2.61, 2.64, 2.60 cm. The mean absolute error is:
hint: Step 1: Find the mean. Step 2: Find |each value − mean|. Step 3: Average those.

sentence: If the mean value is 5.00 s and the mean absolute error is 0.05 s, the percentage error is _______.

title: Error Propagation — The Core Rules

sections.heading: Why Propagation Matters
sections.body:
Derived quantities (density = mass/volume, speed = distance/time) depend on measured values. Errors in each measurement **combine** to give the error in the derived result.

JEE tests this regularly — learn these rules once, use them forever.

sections.heading: Rule 1: Addition & Subtraction
sections.body:
If Z = A + B  or  Z = A − B:

**ΔZ = ΔA + ΔB**

Absolute errors always ADD — regardless of + or − sign.

sections.heading: Rule 2: Multiplication & Division
sections.body:
If Z = A × B  or  Z = A / B:

**ΔZ/Z = ΔA/A + ΔB/B**

Relative errors ADD for both multiplication and division.

sections.heading: Rule 3: Powers
sections.body:
If Z = Aᵖ Bq / Cʳ:

**ΔZ/Z = p(ΔA/A) + q(ΔB/B) + r(ΔC/C)**

The power **multiplies** the relative error of each quantity.

highlight: For Z = A³: ΔZ/Z = 3(ΔA/A). The exponent multiplies the error — this is the most-tested rule in JEE.

title: Error Propagation — Master Formula
formula: Z = AᵖBq/Cʳ  →  ΔZ/Z = p(ΔA/A) + q(ΔB/B) + r(ΔC/C)

parts.meaning: Absolute values of exponents/powers in the formula
Relative error in the derived quantity Z

note: Use ABSOLUTE values of powers even for division (denominator). Never use negative exponents.
derived_from: Take log: ln Z = p·ln A + q·ln B − r·ln C. Differentiate: dZ/Z = p·dA/A + q·dB/B + r·dC/C. For errors, use absolute values.

title: Error Propagation — Quick Reference
instruction: Tap each formula to see the error rule.

ΔZ = ΔA + ΔB
Absolute errors STILL add! (Common trap in JEE)

ΔZ/Z = ΔA/A + ΔB/B

ΔZ/Z = ΔA/A + ΔB/B
Relative errors add for division too.

ΔZ/Z = n × (ΔA/A)
Power multiplies the relative error.

ΔZ/Z = p(ΔA/A) + q(ΔB/B) + r(ΔC/C)
The master formula.

title: Worked Example: Error in Sum & Difference
problem: L₁ = (12.5 ± 0.2) cm and L₂ = (7.3 ± 0.1) cm. Find (a) L₁ + L₂ and (b) L₁ − L₂ with errors.

steps.detail:
L₁ = 12.5 cm,  ΔL₁ = 0.2 cm
L₂ = 7.3 cm,   ΔL₂ = 0.1 cm

Difference = 12.5 − 7.3 = 5.2 cm

Error: ΔZ = ΔL₁ + ΔL₂ = 0.2 + 0.1 = 0.3 cm

Result: **(5.2 ± 0.3) cm**

The error is IDENTICAL in both cases (0.3 cm).

Absolute errors always ADD — whether you add or subtract the quantities. This is the #1 trap in JEE for this topic!

title: Worked Example: Error in Powers — Sphere Volume
problem: Radius of a sphere: r = (2.10 ± 0.05) cm. Find the percentage error in its volume V = (4/3)πr³.

steps.detail:
V = (4/3)πr³

The constant (4/3)π has zero error. Only r contributes.
Power of r = **3**.

ΔV/V = 3 × (Δr/r)

The exponent 3 multiplies the relative error of r.

Percentage error in volume ≈ **7.1%**

💡 The volume error is TRIPLE the radius error because V ∝ r³.
This scaling by powers is the key JEE concept.

question: T = 2π√(L/g). If L has 2% error and g has 3% error, the % error in T is:
explanation:
T = 2π × L^(1/2) × g^(−1/2)

ΔT/T = (1/2)(ΔL/L) + (1/2)(Δg/g)

= (1/2)(2%) + (1/2)(3%) = 1% + 1.5% = **2.5%** ✓

Note: Use |power| = 1/2 for both L and g. Constants 2π have no error.
hint: Rewrite T as L^(1/2) × g^(-1/2). Power of each is 1/2. Apply: ΔT/T = (1/2)(ΔL/L) + (1/2)(Δg/g)
